excerpts.author: realbigsean
excerpts.content: I'm noticing that `engine_newPayloadV2` isn't available prior to the capella fork, but I thought it was supposed to available at least starting at bellatrix so we can use it across the fork transition

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content:
I've noticed some disparity, and maybe I'm missing something. The current consensus spec and spec tests rebase 4844 on top of capella, and go through Capella. Meaning `bellatrx` -> `capella` -> `4844`
The engine API is assuming capella and 4844 are the same fork: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/322/files
If we do that then the actual capella block processing will fail. We will need `ExecutionPayloadV3` to align with the consensus spec

excerpts.author: realbigsean
excerpts.content: That seems right, we should be able to use `engine_newPayloadV2` for serving `ExecutionPayloadV1` + `V2` + `V3` structs though right?

excerpts.author: realbigsean
excerpts.content: I thought the intent here was to decouple endpoint upgrades from struct upgrades (forks)

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: That's fine, we can use `engine_newPayloadV2` to serve `V1`, `V2`, `V3` but we shouldn't add `excessDataGas` to `V2` right? That's my question
